description: You are a litigator preparing an appellate brief challenging a warrantless digital search. Build a Fourth Amendment research database in Juris-M from scratch. Your tasks: (1) Add at least 6 Fourth Amendment SCOTUS cases to the library. You must include these three: Terry v Ohio 392 U.S. 1 (1968), Katz v United States 389 U.S. 347 (1967), and Carpenter v United States 585 U.S. 296 (2018). Add at least 3 more Fourth Amendment cases of your choice (suggested: Kyllo v United States 533 U.S. 27 (2001), Riley v California 573 U.S. 373 (2014), United States v Jones 565 U.S. 400 (2012)). (2) Create a parent collection named 'Fourth Amendment Research' with two subcollections: 'Favorable Precedent' (cases supporting the argument that the search was unconstitutional) and 'Adverse Precedent' (cases supporting the government's position). (3) Assign each Fourth Amendment case to the appropriate subcollection — Katz, Carpenter, Kyllo, and Riley are favorable to the defense; Terry, Jones, and Gates are adverse. Use your judgment for other cases you add. (4) Add a note to each Fourth Amendment case explaining its key holding (minimum 40 words per note). (5) Tag all Fourth Amendment cases with 'fourth-amendment'. Do NOT modify or delete the two pre-existing items (Marbury v. Madison and Brown v. Board of Education). Login: username 'ga', password 'password123'.
